Package com.lemarketjames.reports.overnight

Class OvernightRunner

java.lang.Object
com.lemarketjames.reports.overnight.OvernightRunner
@Component public class OvernightRunner extends Object
Runs each night's overnight reports and records how each run went (LMKT-45). The schedule itself is OvernightScheduleConfig's; this class only knows what a night is, so it can be tested with a fixed clock.

A night is the reports-time-zone day the run time falls on, and its runs cover the trading day before it: the 02:00 run on the 15th reports on the 14th. Jobs run one after another, never in parallel, because the service's connection pool is deliberately small.

  • Method Details

    • runNight

      public void runNight()
      Schedules tonight's run of every overnight report, then runs them. A report that already has a run tonight (the service restarted, or the trigger fired twice) is left alone.

    • catchUp

      public void catchUp()
      At startup: makes sure the most recent night is in the list even if the service was not running at its run time, so the list never just leaves a night out.
      1. Runs left unfinished are failed as interrupted: the service just started, so whatever was running them is gone, and they would otherwise wait forever.
      2. If the most recent run time has passed but its ready-by time has not (a restart at 03:00), the missing reports run now.
      3. If its ready-by time has passed too (a start at 15:00), the missing reports are not run, which would be during trading hours (AC1); each is recorded as failed instead.
      Only the most recent night is checked: a service down for days records only the last one.

    • enforceDeadline

      public void enforceDeadline()
      At the ready-by time: marks LATE every run not finished yet, so the dashboard shows it is missing while it still waits or runs (AC2). Those runs carry on; when one finishes it stays LATE.
